The quick answer

Yes, a Cairo to Alexandria day trip is worth it if you accept the drive. It is about three hours each way along the roughly 220 km desert road, and it buys you the Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, Pompey's Pillar, the Roman theatre at Kom el-Dikka, a museum and a Mediterranean seafood lunch. Sawa's shared day tour is from €47 per person, as listed in November 2026. Skip it only if six hours in a vehicle sounds unbearable.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

You have four or five days in Cairo and one to spare. Everyone tells you the Pyramids, the Grand Egyptian Museum and Islamic Cairo, and then someone mentions Alexandria: sea air, Greek and Roman ruins, a Mediterranean waterfront. Is it realistic, 220 km away? This post answers that honestly: what a Cairo to Alexandria day trip covers, what it costs, how to get there by tour, train, bus or car, and who should stay put. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, lists a Cairo to Alexandria shared day tour, and its team has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Cairo to Alexandria day trip: the short answer

A Cairo to Alexandria day trip is worth it if you want Egypt's Greco-Roman side, sea air after days of desert monuments and seafood on a waterfront, and you accept roughly six hours of driving in one day. It is not worth it if fitting it in means cutting Luxor, Abu Simbel or the Red Sea; those deserve your days more. And if you have two spare days rather than one, an overnight in Alexandria beats the day trip comfortably.

The worth-it test: go if you are (1) based in Cairo with a spare day, (2) happy with an early start and a late-afternoon return, and (3) genuinely curious about Alexander the Great and Cleopatra's Egypt. Two out of three? Sleep on it.

Is Alexandria worth visiting?

Alexandria is worth visiting precisely because it is unlike the rest of Egypt. Alexander the Great founded the city in 331 BC, and under his successors, the Ptolemies, it became the Mediterranean's intellectual capital, famous for the ancient Library and for the Lighthouse of Pharos, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

What you visit today is layered rather than monumental. The Bibliotheca Alexandrina, opened in 2002, is the modern successor to the ancient Library. The Citadel of Qaitbay, a Mamluk fortress built between 1477 and 1479, stands on the ruins of the ancient Lighthouse. Beneath the streets lie the Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, and nearby is the Roman theatre at Kom el-Dikka. Above them sits Egypt's second city and chief port, wrapped around its eastern harbour by a long corniche (seafront promenade). By the sea it is cooler than Cairo in summer, and winter days can be breezy and wet.

What you can see in Alexandria in one day

Four to five hours on the ground comfortably covers the Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, Pompey's Pillar, the Roman theatre at Kom el-Dikka and one museum, plus a seafood lunch. In sightseeing order:

  1. Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa. Burial chambers cut into the rock on three levels from the 2nd century AD and rediscovered in 1900, when a donkey is said to have fallen into the access shaft. You descend a spiral staircase to reliefs blending Egyptian gods with Roman dress: Anubis appears as a Roman soldier. It is the one Alexandria sight every visitor remembers.
  2. Pompey's Pillar. A granite column about 27 m tall including its base and capital, raised between AD 298 and 302 in honour of the emperor Diocletian (the name Pompey comes from a medieval misreading). It stands in the enclosure of the Serapeum, the great temple of Serapis, and is the only ancient monument in Alexandria still standing where it was built.
  3. Roman theatre at Kom el-Dikka. Sawa's listing calls it the Roman Amphitheatre. Polish archaeologists from the University of Warsaw began excavating it in the 1960s, and 13 tiers of seating survive, for an audience of about 600.
  4. National Museum of Alexandria. The city's story under one roof, from the pharaonic and Greco-Roman periods onwards.
  5. Citadel of Qaitbay. A Mamluk fortress raised in the 1470s on the ruins of the ancient Lighthouse, guarding the eastern harbour. It is open from 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM, according to the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities.
  6. Bibliotheca Alexandrina. The 2002 successor to the ancient Library: a tilted disc of a building facing the sea, holding exhibition halls, museums and a planetarium.

Note: the Sawa shared tour visits the first four sights, with lunch at a local restaurant, which is the Greco-Roman core. The Citadel and the Bibliotheca are not on its set itinerary. Travellers set on both should plan a second, self-guided day, and the Library especially rewards unhurried time.

Cairo to Alexandria: the shape of the day on the shared tour

The shared tour day runs about ten hours, hotel to hotel. Here is the order of the day on the Cairo to Alexandria Mediterranean Day Tour, as listed in November 2026:

  1. Early pickup in Cairo. Hotel pickup is included.
  2. The desert road to the coast. About three hours.
  3. Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa. The city's most atmospheric site, and the first stop.
  4. Pompey's Pillar. The Serapeum column.
  5. National Museum of Alexandria, with lunch at a local restaurant.
  6. The Roman theatre, then the drive back along the desert road.
  7. Drop-off at your Cairo hotel in the late afternoon or early evening.

How to get from Cairo to Alexandria: tour, train, bus or car

You have four realistic ways to cover the distance: an organised tour door to door, the railway, an intercity coach, or a private car with driver. Road and rail take broadly similar times; what differs is what is handled for you.

Option Time each way Who it suits What to know
Shared day tour About 3 hours First-timers who want guide, tickets and lunch handled From €47 per person, as listed in November 2026; hotel pickup, tickets, lunch and a licensed guide included
Train (Egyptian National Railways) About 2.5 to 3 hours Independent travellers starting from central Cairo Seat 61's 2026 timetable has a Talgo at 08:00 from Ramses arriving at 10:30, a VIP train at 08:10 arriving at 11:15 and an express at 12:00 arriving at 14:50; foreigner fares are US$50 first or US$40 second on the Talgo and US$40 or US$35 on VIP or Express
Intercity coach About 3 to 3.5 hours Budget travellers staying overnight Departures from Tahrir Square, Nasr City and Heliopolis; 12Go listed coach tickets at roughly US$10 to US$15 on 8 November 2026
Private car with driver About 2.5 to 3.5 hours, traffic permitting Families and custom routes The only option where you set the sightseeing list, so you can add the Citadel and the Bibliotheca; get a quote from the operator

On the train, foreigners pay separate dollar fares, and the national railway's website and app sell Egyptian-price tickets to Egyptians only. Foreigners buy at the foreigner office at Ramses or through an agency, and the main Alexandria station is Alexandria Misr. Self-driving is possible, but the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) says accidents are common because of variable road conditions, dangerous driving and poor traffic law enforcement, and parking in Alexandria is a headache, so it is a rare choice for first-time visitors. The train suits travellers staying overnight; the shared tour suits anyone who must be back in Cairo the same evening with everything handled.

Costs and budget for an Alexandria day trip

Booked as a shared departure, the whole day is from €47 per person, as listed in November 2026, and the listing includes transport, a licensed guide, entrance tickets and lunch. The price is fixed per traveller, however the group fills. The main extra is tips: a tip for the guide and driver is customary and not included, so carry small Egyptian pound notes.

  • Shared tour: from €47 per person, including hotel pickup and drop-off, entrance tickets, lunch and guide, as listed in November 2026.
  • DIY day: train or coach fare plus individual entrance tickets, lunch and city transport. The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities lists foreign adult tickets at EGP 200 each for the Catacombs, Pompey's Pillar and the Roman theatre and EGP 220 for the National Museum, EGP 820 in all (about €14 at EGP 60 to the euro, the rate on 8 November 2026), and EGP 200 for the Citadel of Qaitbay (about €3.30). The list is the Ministry's 5 November 2024 edition, so check current prices before you go.
  • Bibliotheca Alexandrina: the visitor page does not publish admission prices, so check at the library before visiting.

On cost, the shared tour usually wins for solo travellers and pairs: splitting a van, guide and tickets across a group beats a private car and guide priced per vehicle, especially for parties of one or two.

Insider tips and common mistakes

Plan around two things most first-timers miss, the Bibliotheca's Friday closure and the sheer length of the drive, and the day falls into place. Seven tips from our team:

  • Never plan the Library for a Friday. The Bibliotheca Alexandrina is closed on Fridays; visits run 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM Sunday to Thursday and 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM on Saturday (checked 8 November 2026).
  • Honour the early start. Leaving Cairo early is what makes a one-day trip work, and the Library closes at 5:00 PM.
  • Bring layers. The coast is cooler and breezier than Cairo, a relief in summer and bracing in winter.
  • Mind the spiral staircase. The Catacombs are reached on foot down a tight spiral stair; travellers with knee, heart or mobility issues can wait above ground.
  • Eat the seafood. Alexandria is Egypt's seafood capital, and lunch at a local restaurant is part of the shared tour; mention dietary needs when you reserve.
  • Don't overstuff the day. Four sights plus lunch is a full, happy day; adding the Citadel and Library interiors means staying overnight.
  • Check the itinerary before booking. Alexandria itineraries vary by operator, so confirm exactly which sights yours includes.

The verdict on the Cairo to Alexandria day trip

Go, if you have a spare Cairo day and any curiosity about Greco-Roman Egypt or the Mediterranean. One well-planned day covers the Catacombs, Pompey's Pillar, a museum and the Roman theatre, with the drive folded into an air-conditioned van. faq.q: Is a day trip from Cairo to Alexandria worth the long drive?
faq.a: For most travellers with a spare day in Cairo, yes. The drive is about three hours each way, but the tour folds it into one air-conditioned block each way, and what waits, the Catacombs, Pompey's Pillar and the Mediterranean, is the side of Egypt you cannot see in Cairo or Luxor. Skip it only if six hours in a vehicle is genuinely a deal-breaker.

faq.q: Can you visit the Bibliotheca Alexandrina on a day trip?
faq.a: Yes, with planning. The library is closed on Fridays and its visits, museums and planetarium run 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM Sunday to Thursday and 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM on Saturday (checked 8 November 2026). It is not on the shared tour's set itinerary, so take an early train and plan your own visit, or add it on a second day in the city.

faq.q: Is the train better than driving to Alexandria?
faq.a: Time-wise they are close: the train from Cairo takes about 2.5 to 3 hours against roughly 3 hours by road. The train suits independent travellers starting from central Cairo and staying overnight; the tour suits anyone who wants tickets, lunch, a guide and hotel pickup handled, and needs to be back in Cairo the same evening.

faq.q: How much time do you actually get in Alexandria?
faq.a: About four to five hours on the ground out of a ten-hour day. That is enough for the Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa, Pompey's Pillar, the National Museum and the Roman theatre, and a seafood lunch. It is not enough to also tour the Citadel interior and the Bibliotheca properly; those want an overnight.

faq.q: Can solo travellers join without paying a supplement?
faq.a: On Sawa, yes. The price is fixed per traveller with no solo surcharge, so you pay the same as someone travelling as a couple. Shared departures of four to eight travellers give you a ready-made group for the day. Read what a shared departure is .

faq.q: What happens if the departure never reaches four travellers?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. Reserving a seat is free, and a 10% deposit is taken only when a date reaches four travellers and gets the GoAhead. A date has until seven days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing and Sawa suggests another date. Once confirmed, a departure is not cancelled for low numbers, and if a traveller fails to pay the balance they are excluded and the tour still runs.
